Oven-Fried Wings with Family Sauce Finishes

Salt and baking powder help oven wings turn golden without a deep fryer. Finish the adult plate with Buffalo and Ghost Pepper, and the kids' wings with butter and bottled Parmesan Garlic sauce.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME90 min oven time
COOK METHODOven
EST. / SERVING~650 cal | ~55g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Use baking powder, not baking soda, and keep the ratio at 1 tsp salt plus 1/2 tbsp baking powder per pound of wings.

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 1 lb chicken wing flats and drumettes (scale the seasoning ratio for more)
  • 1 tsp salt per pound of wings
  • 1/2 tbsp baking powder per pound of wings (not baking soda)
  • Kinder's Buttery Buffalo Wing Sauce, to taste

Ingredients — continued

  • Melinda's Ghost Pepper Wing Sauce, to taste
  • Butter and bottled Parmesan Garlic sauce, to taste, for the kids' finish
  • Carrot and celery sticks, to serve
  • For the blue-cheese dressing: 150g 2% cottage cheese, 113g blue cheese, 30g fat-free ultra-filtered milk, 1 tsp lemon juice, 1 tsp salt/pepper/garlic seasoning, and 1 tbsp fresh chives

Allergens: dairy.

You want wing-night crunch without a deep fryer and a mild finish for kids alongside sauces for adults.

Method

  1. 1.SEASON THE WINGS. Coat the wings evenly with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tbsp baking powder per pound. Baking powder helps the skin brown; do not substitute baking soda.
  2. 2.BAKE ON A RACK. Arrange the wings in one layer on a wire rack over a baking tray. Bake at 450°F for 45 minutes, flip, then bake another 45 minutes. This is the creator's method; ovens and wing sizes vary. Check that the thickest meat reaches 165°F without touching bone, and adjust the time as needed.
  3. 3.MAKE THE FAMILY FINISHES. For the adult plate, toss four wings with Kinder's Buffalo and four with Melinda's Ghost Pepper, or sauce to taste. For the kids' portion, mix butter with bottled Parmesan Garlic sauce. Amounts were not measured; add gradually to taste.
  4. 4.BLEND THE BLUE-CHEESE DRESSING. Blend the cottage cheese, milk, lemon juice and seasoning. Pulse in most of the blue cheese, then fold in the rest and the chives. Chill 10–15 minutes. This makes eight dressing portions.
  5. 5.SERVE. Add carrots and celery. Use one-eighth of the dressing batch for the pictured adult plate; serve other family portions to appetite. The approximate macros below do not apply to the kids' portions.

Keys to success

  • 450°F for 45 minutes per side is the creator's method, not a universal guarantee. Verify 165°F in the thickest meat without touching bone; cooking time varies.
  • Do not imply that the internal temperature was measured in the video.

Storage and reheating

Store: Refrigerate leftover cooked wings and dressing promptly in separate covered containers. Follow ingredient package guidance and local food-safety recommendations for storage times.

Reheat: Reheat wings in an oven or air fryer until hot throughout, watching closely so the skin does not over-brown. Reheat sauce separately if needed and use fresh vegetables.

Lasts: The package does not specify a tested storage duration; follow current food-safety guidance and discard leftovers that have been left out too long.

Estimated nutrition

~650 cal | ~55g protein.

Conditional estimate for the pictured adult eight-wing plate: approximately 650 calories and 55g protein. It assumes about 200g cooked edible wing meat and skin excluding bones, roughly 1 tbsp each of Buffalo and Ghost Pepper sauce, one-eighth of the blue-cheese dressing batch, and an unweighed vegetable side. The wings were not weighed, and the standard Kinder's nutrition label checked is not a verified match for the organic Buffalo SKU shown. Sauce amounts and brands change the result. This is not a measured or exact nutrition panel; fat and carbohydrate totals are not published. No kid-plate macros are supplied.
